what_it_checks: that a group with only one target is NOT quarantined on a single failure, so a lone provider is never taken out of service by a transient error
that under high traffic with every target healthy, none is quarantined: the failure-rate rule does not fire on volume alone
that a rate-limit rejection is retried immediately against a healthy sibling target rather than waited out
that the retry loop still honours the overall timeout when every sibling is also rate-limited
that a request whose primary target fails is served by the declared fallback target and the caller still gets an answer
that a per-target quarantine duration is honoured for exactly as long as configured
that a target whose request quota is exhausted is excluded from the candidate set before dispatch, not dispatched to and rejected
which targets are still eligible given the current request and token counters
that a price-ranking placement really selects the cheapest eligible target
that price ranking is applied only to targets that still have request and token headroom
end to end, that once a provider's spend cap is reached its targets stop being selected
end to end, that a per-target spend cap removes that target specifically while its siblings keep serving
that when capacity frees up the more urgent waiting request is served before the less urgent one
that a waiting request that gives up is removed from the wait set and does not leak: the bounded-resource property of queueing
that the online policy's learned per-target state is capped, so memory does not grow with traffic
that an online selection policy converges onto the better-performing model rather than oscillating
